threats.title: Customer Account Spoofing
threats.description: An attacker could impersonate a legitimate customer to place fraudulent orders or access their order history.

threats.title: Staff Account Spoofing
threats.description: An attacker could impersonate staff to manipulate order statuses, access sales reports, or modify menu items and application configurations.

threats.title: Web Application Server Spoofing
threats.description: An attacker might set up a fraudulent web server to phish user credentials or intercept sensitive data.

threats.title: Order Data Tampering
threats.description: An attacker could modify order details (e.g., items, quantities, prices, status) in transit or at rest.

threats.title: Menu Data Tampering
threats.description: An attacker could alter menu item data (e.g., prices or descriptions) before it is stored in the database.

threats.title: Sales Report Tampering
threats.description: Unauthorized individuals could alter sales data in the MongoDB Database, leading to falsified reports.

threats.title: Application Code/Configuration Tampering
threats.description: Malicious modification of the application’s source code, server configurations, or environment variables could introduce backdoors or disable security features.

threats.title: Fraudulent Order Repudiation
threats.description: A customer could deny placing an order if insufficient logging and non-repudiation controls are in place.

threats.title: Staff Action Repudiation
threats.description: Staff members (Barista, Manager, Administrator) could deny performing actions if audit logs are insufficient, not immutable, or can be tampered with.

threats.title: Customer PII Disclosure
threats.description: Unauthorized access to customer names, contact details, delivery addresses, and order history.

threats.title: Staff Credential Disclosure
threats.description: Exposure of usernames, passwords, or session tokens for staff members due to insecure storage or unencrypted transmission.

threats.title: Application Code and Configuration Disclosure
threats.description: Exposure of source code, server configurations, environment variables, or API keys.

threats.title: Sales Data Disclosure
threats.description: Unauthorized access to sales reports or underlying aggregated sales data.

threats.title: Web Application Server DoS
threats.description: An attacker could flood the Web Application Server with excessive requests, making it unavailable.

threats.title: MongoDB Database DoS
threats.description: Malicious or poorly optimized queries could overload the database, making it unresponsive.

threats.title: Customer to Staff Privilege Escalation
threats.description: A customer could exploit a vulnerability to gain unauthorized access to Barista, Manager, or Administrator functionalities.

threats.title: Barista/Manager to Administrator Privilege Escalation
threats.description: A Barista or Manager could exploit a vulnerability to gain Administrator privileges.

threats.title: Horizontal Privilege Escalation
threats.description: Gaining unauthorized access to another user’s account within the same privilege level.

data.name:
Client Zone
(Untrusted)
data.description: Client side is untrusted, therefore all input originating from here must be validated on the server. The web application server trusts the client for basic UI interactions but not for data integrity or authorization decisions.

data.name:
Third-Party Zone
(Partially Trusted)
data.description: Third-party services are external and partially trusted; communication channels are secured, but data received from them is validated.

data.name:
Database Zone
(Trusts Web App Server)
data.description: The MongoDB database server trusts calls from the web application server’s identity.

data.name: 1.1 Submit order details
data.description: Data flow 1 – Customer Places an Order, step 1.1: Customer selects items, customizes them, and submits the order details to the Web Application Server.

data.name: 1.3 Payment request
data.description: Data flow 1 – Customer Places an Order, step 1.3: Web Application Server initiates a payment request, sending tokenized payment information to the Payment Gateway (a third-party service).

data.name: 1.4 Transaction response
data.description: Data flow 1 – Customer Places an Order, step 1.4: Payment Gateway processes the payment and sends a transaction response (success/failure) back to the Web Application Server.

data.name: 1.5 Record order & payment
data.description: Data flow 1 – Customer Places an Order, step 1.5: If payment is successful, the Web Application Server records the new order details and payment status in the MongoDB Database.

data.name: 1.7 Order confirmation
data.description: Data flow 1 – Customer Places an Order, step 1.7: Web Application Server sends an order confirmation and status update back to the Customer.

data.name: 2.1 Request incoming orders
data.description: Data flow 2 – Barista Updates Order Status, step 2.1: Barista logs into the staff interface and requests to view incoming orders from the Web Application Server.

data.name: 2.2 Query order data
data.description: Data flow 2 – Barista Updates Order Status, step 2.2: Web Application Server authenticates and authorizes the Barista, then queries the MongoDB Database for relevant order data.

data.name: 2.3 Pending order data
data.description: Data flow 2 – Barista Updates Order Status, step 2.3: MongoDB Database retrieves the pending order data and sends it to the Web Application Server.

data.name: 2.4 Order list
data.description: Data flow 2 – Barista Updates Order Status, step 2.4: Web Application Server sends the order list to the Barista for display.

data.name: 2.6 Updated order status
data.description: Data flow 2 – Barista Updates Order Status, step 2.6: Barista sends the updated order status (e.g., from “Received” to “Preparing”) to the Web Application Server.

data.name: 2.7 Update order record
data.description: Data flow 2 – Barista Updates Order Status, step 2.7: Web Application Server validates the status update and updates the order record in the MongoDB Database.

data.name: 3.1 Request sales reports
data.description: Data flow 3 – Manager Accesses Basic Sales Reports, step 3.1: Manager logs into the staff interface and requests to view basic sales reports from the Web Application Server.

data.name: 3.2 Query sales data
data.description: Data flow 3 – Manager Accesses Basic Sales Reports, step 3.2: Web Application Server authenticates and authorizes the Manager, then queries the MongoDB Database for aggregated sales data.

data.name: 3.3 Aggregated sales data
data.description: Data flow 3 – Manager Accesses Basic Sales Reports, step 3.3: MongoDB Database retrieves the requested sales data and sends it back to the Web Application Server.

data.name: 3.4 Sales report
data.description: Data flow 3 – Manager Accesses Basic Sales Reports, step 3.4: Web Application Server processes the sales data (e.g., calculates totals, formats for display) and sends it as a response to the Manager.

data.name: 4.2 Submit new menu item
data.description: Data flow 4 – Administrator Adds New Menu Item, step 4.2: Administrator inputs details for a new menu item (name, description, price, etc.) and submits the information to the Web Application Server.

data.name: 4.4 Create menu item
data.description: Data flow 4 – Administrator Adds New Menu Item, step 4.4: Web Application Server sends the validated new menu item data to the MongoDB Database for creation.

data.name: 4.6 Menu item confirmation
data.description: Data flow 4 – Administrator Adds New Menu Item, step 4.6: Web Application Server sends a confirmation of the successful menu item addition back to the Administrator.
